subject.title: [Feature]: Add TTL/Expiry for Delivery Queue Messages

question: What outbound delivery expiry policy should OpenClaw expose for queued recovery: which config key, default behavior, and expired-entry action?
rationale: The source-level gap is clear, but the fix adds public config and may change whether existing queued messages replay after upgrade.

options.title: Opt-in messages.delivery TTL
options.body: Add optional messages.delivery.maxAgeMs with a failed/quarantine-style expired action, preserving the current no-TTL default while covering startup and reconnect drains.

options.title: Finite default TTL
options.body: Ship a default max age to prevent stale floods without user setup, accepting a compatibility-sensitive change to existing recovery behavior.

options.title: Broader freshness design
options.body: Pause the outbound-only fix and design outbound plus inbound stale-message policy together, reducing drift but delaying the known outbound repair.

recommendation.title: Opt-in messages.delivery TTL
recommendation.body: Add optional messages.delivery.maxAgeMs with a failed/quarantine-style expired action, preserving the current no-TTL default while covering startup and reconnect drains.

likelyOwner.reason: Peter Steinberger has the strongest current-history and issue-discussion connection to the recovery/config policy decision.
